chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Kansas City as a hotbed for saxophonists and visiting bands
summary: Goodwin says any visiting star could find an equal in Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It's funny you know when you think of it, he had a different sound, you know, playing out of the corner of his mouth, different sound for that day and of course later Charlie Parker came along and he had a different sound. Kansas City was really the city for saxophone players, wasn't

It was not only the city for saxophone players, it was the roots of what we now call Kansas City jazz. It was a place where it was a hot bed for musicians. I mean, I don't care where you come from or whatever you played, you would find somebody in Kansas City who would play just as much or maybe more than anybody that you could send here because I remember all the big bands, Benny Goodman, everybody --

-- we had a little paddle for each individual that come here because there was always somebody here and if you believed you were a great one, well you could find a great one right here in Kansas City to match up with you.
You can do that right now.
